mapping.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space (def-sr-affine-minkowski-model) and let I be an order-convex subset of R with at least two elements (def-interval); a curve of the model is a map x: I -> A. (a) Derivative and regularity of the parametrization. For s in I and h nonzero with s + h in I the difference quotient (x(s+h) - x(s))/h is an element of V, the displacement from x(s) to x(s+h) divided by the real number h; the curve is differentiable at s when the limit of these quotients as h -> 0 exists in the finite-dimensional real vector space V, and then this limit, written x'(s) in V, is the tangent vector of x at s. If x_A: A -> R^4 is the chart of an inertial frame (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart), then x is differentiable at s exactly when the R^4-valued map x_A o x is differentiable at s in the sense of def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral, and then x'(s) = E((x_A o x)'(s)), where E: R^4 -> V is the frame isomorphism; this does not depend on the inertial chart used, because inertial chart transitions are affine, hence smooth (lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas), and all norms on the finite-dimensional V give the same limit. The curve is C^1 when it is differentiable at every point of I and the derivative map s |-> x'(s), I -> V, is continuous (def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity); it is C^k for k >= 1 when x' is C^{k-1}. A curve on a compact interval [a,b] contained in I is piecewise C^1 when there is a finite partition a = s_0 < s_1 < ... < s_m = b such that x is C^1 on every open subinterval (s_{i-1},s_i) and the one-sided derivatives at the s_i exist; derivatives at the endpoints of I are the one-sided limits over I. (b) Causal character. Let x be differentiable at s in I. Then x is regular at s if x'(s) is not the zero vector; x is timelike (respectively null, spacelike, causal) at s if the vector x'(s) is timelike (respectively null, spacelike, causal) in the sense of def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, and x is future-directed at s if x'(s) is future timelike or future null in the sense of def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets. The zero vector has no causal character, so only a regular curve has a causal character at s. (c) Worldlines. A future timelike worldline (massive worldline) is a C^1 curve x: I -> A with x'(s) future timelike for every s in I; a future causal curve (respectively a future null curve) is a C^1 curve with x'(s) future causal (respectively future null) for every s in I. A piecewise C^1 worldline is a piecewise C^1 curve all of whose one-sided tangents are future timelike, and a C^k worldline is a worldline whose parametrization is C^k; C^2 regularity is what makes the four-acceleration of this page available. The parametrization is part of the curve: the image of a future timelike worldline is also the image of the past-directed curve s |-> x(-s), which is not a worldline of this model, and no worldline or clock claim is attached to it. The definition asserts the existence of no worldline beyond those given by an explicit formula.

mapping.statement: Let c > 0 be a fixed real number (the conversion constant of the model, whose physical interpretation is supplied with the model's coordinate conventions) and let x: I -> A be a C^1 future timelike worldline (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline). Then the function g_x: I -> R, g_x(s) := -eta(x'(s),x'(s)), is continuous and strictly positive: continuity holds because in an eta-orthonormal basis eta(x'(s),x'(s)) = sum_{a,b} eta_ab (x'(s))^a (x'(s))^b is a finite sum of products of continuous real functions (lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis, thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions), and positivity is the future timelike hypothesis (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors). Hence u |-> sqrt(g_x(u)) is continuous on I (thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives, thm-composition-of-continuous-functions) and Riemann integrable on every compact subinterval of I (thm-continuous-implies-integrable). For s_0, s in I the proper time from s_0 to s is tau(s) := c^{-1} integral_{s_0}^{s} sqrt(-eta(x'(u),x'(u))) du, the integral being the oriented integral of def-oriented-integral; explicitly, for a < b in I, tau(b) - tau(a) = c^{-1} integral_a^b sqrt(-eta(x'(u),x'(u))) du, and changing the base point s_0 changes tau by an additive constant. tau depends on the parametrized history of x and on the parameter values; its invariance under increasing C^1 reparametrizations is proved in lem-sr-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance. For the straight future timelike segment x(s) = p + (s - s_0)(q - p) one has tau(b) - tau(a) = c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(q-p,q-p)) (b - a), which is the straight-segment proper time of the model's coordinate conventions. The construction is restricted to future timelike worldlines: at a null point the integrand vanishes, for a spacelike curve -eta(x',x') is negative and the square root is not a real number, and for a past-directed timelike curve the integral is defined but is not attached to a worldline of the model.
mapping.strategy: Definition item with well-definedness obligations: (i) the integrand is the composition of the continuous map s |-> x'(s), the continuous quadratic form v |-> -eta(v,v) (checked in coordinates in an eta-orthonormal basis, since eta is bilinear on the finite-dimensional V) and the continuous power t |-> t^{1/2} on (0,inf); (ii) strict positivity of g_x is exactly the future timelike hypothesis, so the square root is a positive real number on all of I; (iii) existence of the integral on compact subintervals is thm-continuous-implies-integrable, and the oriented convention makes tau(s_0) = 0 and reverses the sign when the endpoints are exchanged; (iv) the base point enters only additively, so elapsed times between parameter values are intrinsic; (v) the straight-segment consistency is a direct evaluation: x' is constant on a straight segment and the integrand is c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(q-p,q-p)) times the parameter length. No choice principle is used. The item deliberately does not assert that tau is differentiable or invertible (that is lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization) nor that a physical clock reads tau (that belongs to the adopted physical interpretation).

mapping.statement: Let c > 0 and let (A,V,eta,C^+) be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space. (a) Norm of the four-velocity. Let n in V be future unit timelike, eta(n,n) = -1, and put n^perp := {v in V : eta(n,v) = 0}. Moreover |w| := sqrt(eta(w,w)) defines a norm on n^perp. (d) Relative velocity and Lorentz factor. Let n and u be future unit timelike vectors, put gamma := -eta(n,u) and w := c h(u)/gamma. Then gamma >= 1, w lies in n^perp, u = gamma (n + w/c), |w|^2 = c^2 (1 - gamma^{-2}) < c^2, gamma = (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, and gamma = 1 if and only if u = n.
